changes: Date: the chronogram gives only NS 76x. The units word is lost in the lacuna, rasa = 6 (tens) and śaila = 7 (hundreds). Year changed to '76x' and ce_approx to 1640–1649 instead of the single year 1645.
Date: noted that 'śukle' conflicts with 'kṛṣṇāṣṭamī'. Pakṣa kept as kṛṣṇa; month left empty.
Scribe: confidence lowered to medium. The plural 'alikhan' and the damaged 'śrīmān‥ maḥ' may hide a second scribe or a longer name.
Notes: the identification with Jagatprakāśa Malla is now marked as probable, not certain. The name is kept as written.

date.as_written: ‥‥‥ (rasa)śaile ca gate nepālavatsare | śukle kṛṣṇāṣṭamī bhaume

notes: Chronogram: the units word is lost in the lacuna before '(rasa)'. Read right to left, śaila = 7 (hundreds) and rasa = 6 (tens), so the year is NS 76x (CE 1640–1649). This fits the catalogue's 'NS 76?'. 'Prakāśamalla' is probably Jagatprakāśa Malla of Bhaktapur, who reigned from about NS 764 (CE 1644). If so, the copy dates to NS 764–769 (CE 1644–1649). The colophon itself has only 'prakāśamalla', so the name is kept as written. Date: 'śukle kṛṣṇāṣṭamī' contradicts itself. 'śukle' could be a corruption of 'śukre' (the month Śukra = Jyeṣṭha), or 'kṛṣṇāṣṭamī' could name the festival, so the month is left empty. Scribe: 'alikhan' is plural and is followed by the damaged 'śrīmān‥ maḥ', so a second scribe (e.g. ‥rāma) or a longer name may be lost. '(syākhe tvarānvitaḥ)' is unclear. Bhaktapur is taken as the place of copying because it is named as the realm ruled by the king.
